notes: Lead profile: SMB (support SaaS), 80 employees, US HQ. Building a lightweight agent to triage incoming support tickets and create/update tickets in their DB.
Primary ask: hosted API that they can trial without procurement. Emphasis on fast time-to-value and low integration friction.

Use-case details (customer quotes): "We need TL;DRs and structured JSON outputs to populate our ticket fields — priority, intent, suggested SLA — and ability to call a ticketing API to open/assign tickets."

Latency/throughput: interactive-turn latency target ~<200ms median for short summaries; bulk nightly summarization acceptable in batch. Estimated 2k-6k tickets/day initially, spiking to 15k/day in 6 months.

Model preference: open to mid-sized open models; wants Redwood curated variants and a clearly documented fallback policy. Cost sensitivity: high — wants guidance on batching, caching and token controls.
Security: require SSO (SAML) for Console access, SOC2 attestation, audit logs for generated outputs. Data residency not strict — US public cloud ok.
Integration notes: uses Intercom + Postgres + a lightweight node microservice for webhooks. Wants function-calling to push ticket events and JSON structured output for CRM mapping.

POC ask: give sandbox API keys, a sample prompt/template library, and instructions to enable function-calls in the hosted sandbox. Customer will supply ~1k anonymized tickets and a mapping of ticket fields.

Sales notes: warm lead from self-serve signup; likely conversion if POC shows consistent latency and cost guidance. Suggest quick checklist: sandbox keys, SE POC session, security FAQ answers, template mapping guide.
Quote from call: "If we can auto-summarize and auto-fill fields at >80% accuracy, we can reduce agent triage by 30%."
